artifacts.summary: Confirms the Containment gap is real and currently live for ~12 unmigrated extension implementation agents; recommends layering the Containment predicate onto git-commit-scoped.sh's existing --task flag and reusing reserved exit code 7 (success-with-drops) plus folding all-dropped into existing exit 4, with drop-and-warn/fail-open posture matching the two existing (but non-reaching) Containment implementations.

memory_candidates.content: Anti-pattern found in this codebase: a prose instruction in one agent definition pointing at a "self-check" section in another agent's file, where that section was later mechanized into a wrapper script the pointing agent never calls. The cross-reference silently goes dead (the check structurally cannot run) while still reading as if it's enforced. When migrating a prose check into a mechanized wrapper, grep every other caller that still points at the prose section, not just the one being migrated.

In this codebase's commit pipeline, when a new per-task predicate needs to run inside git-commit-scoped.sh and most live callers already pass --task <N> for the unrelated V5 contention check, layering the new predicate onto that same flag (rather than adding a new opt-in flag) retrofits protection onto every existing call site with zero call-site edits. Check first whether any caller wants one predicate without the other before assuming a single shared flag is safe.
